Capture date: 2026-11-12
Salesforce CLI: 2.156.8
Orgs: seven new Developer scratch orgs with 30-day lifetimes. One had PersonAccounts enabled. All seven were deleted. For each deletion the active scratch record count changed from one to zero and the local target ceased to resolve.
API versions: 62.0 and 67.0. Apex helpers and @IsTest classes were redeployed at each source API, and ApexClass.ApiVersion was verified after each deployment. Anonymous execution and test invocation also specified that API.
Coverage: 63 case expressions, each at both API versions via anonymous Apex and @IsTest (252 observations). Each of the 63 case quartets agrees across its four routes. The original name panels contain 29 initials and 30 surname subcases. The first calibration has four initials and 38 surname inputs. A fourth scratch org supplied 162 keyboard, 122 prefix and 148 holdout inputs. A fifth scratch org tested 80 unseen boundary inputs against predictions frozen before native execution. All 80 agreed at both APIs on both routes, including 20 saves, 38 contacts at 97, four at 98 and 18 at 100. The sixth org exercised 36 Lead name cases and the Title-filtered Contact Phone rule using real DML and lookup. The seventh org supplied 74 local edit inputs for short extensions, terminal triple rotations, neighboring swaps and near misses. Negative controls and intentionally repeated pairs are included in panel totals.
Manifest: cases.json gives group, case name and Apex expression. The .cls files are the complete synthetic helpers. The test method and anonymous wrappers evaluate the same expression in a fresh transaction, then report its value with an intentional assertion.
Transport: typed AssertException, case marker, Test.isRunningTest() route, expected payload length and closing marker. Reject CLI failure before the observation, incomplete method lists, missing/partial payloads, and Apex log truncation/exhaustion diagnostics. Each request rolls back its DML. Record IDs were compared inside Apex and replaced by seed labels or integer positions. No external IDs assigned by Salesforce were exported.
Projects: business, extra, names, bound and limit use the default business-account org. Calibration uses another plain Developer org. Keyboard, prefix and holdout use the default Contact rule in the fourth org. The fifth org uses that rule for the keyboardBoundary group. The localEdits group uses the default Contact rule in the seventh org. The leadNames group uses the default Lead rule on records with distinct Companies. The phoneCriteria group additionally deploys only the Contact Phone rule and Title filter under criteria/. These panels compare real Find and DML for pairs isolated by exact first name and a per-pair email. Extra deploys the owned external ID and assigns the included permission set. The baseline person search has no active Person Account duplicate rule. Custom and personActive include the active Contact and Person Account matching and duplicate rules in this fixture. PersonInactive and order were run after deactivating only the custom Person Account duplicate rule. The standard Person Account rule remained inactive throughout.
Membership: sorted labels preserve membership and multiplicity but do not represent return order. The limit rows additionally compare seed ordinal with sorted ID rank. The last exact seed was omitted on both the Find and save-error routes. Name-panel confidences are observed integers. Save verdicts describe transaction-local state; no report row was observed after commit.
